title: Kernel-matcher and gated-commit protocol with fallback playbook
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a runtime-level "arbiter" that performs kernel-to-model matchmaking and a gated-commit protocol for speculative decoding. The arbiter computes a compact acceptance score for early-output candidates and decides whether to let tentative tokens be committed to the caller or to reroute the request to a higher-fidelity path. The design emphasizes low-overhead kernel matching (fast kernel selection based on fingerprint heuristics), attention-window micro-optimizations for short prefixes, and a staged fallback playbook that minimizes user-visible rollbacks.

Background and motivation:
We have multiple model variants and kernel implementations with different latency/cost/quality tradeoffs. Existing speculative pipelines commit early outputs without a standardized acceptance signal and sometimes require jarring rollbacks when the downstream coherence is poor. This leads to user-visible quality regressions and opaque cost spikes when we switch to expensive fallbacks. The arbiter aims to make the decision deterministic, measurable, and tunable.

Goals:
- Define an acceptance protocol that is computable within <200 microseconds post-prefill and correlates with downstream quality and token-level agreement.
- Match models to kernels using a lightweight fingerprint to reduce kernel-selection overhead for short and medium-length sequences.
- Provide a staged fallback that soft-commits token prefixes when safe and uses a splice/patch mechanism to correct outputs with minimal disruption.
- Instrument telemetry and SLOs to track early-commit precision, rollback cost, and fallback frequency.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change model training or tokenization rules.
- We do not replace the full routing layer; this is a local decisioning component embedded in the serving runtime.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Kernel matcher: compute a kernel fingerprint for the model + sequence-length cohort using micro-benchmarks cached per (model, seq_bucket, device). The matcher selects the kernel variant with an estimated latency and memory score. If estimated latency exceeds per-customer SLO, route to a different model tier.

2) Gated-commit acceptance: after prefill and one or two decode steps, generate an acceptance vector composed of: (a) normalized top-logit gap (NLG), (b) attention sparsity delta (ASD) relative to baseline, (c) kernel confidence score (KCS) derived from kernel performance variance, and (d) historical per-route calibration offset. A lightweight logistic model maps this vector to acceptance probability p_accept.

3) Commit policy: if p_accept >= fast_commit_threshold (configurable by route and customer tier) then emit tokens immediately (fast path). If p_accept in [soft_commit_min, fast_commit_threshold) then emit tokens tagged as "soft-committed": visible to caller but recorded with a retractable anchor. If p_accept < soft_commit_min then hold output and reroute to fallback.

4) Fallback playbook: the fallback chain is: (a) secondary kernel variant (same model), (b) higher-capacity model variant on same hardware, (c) dedicated-run (reserved capacity) or regionally proxied model. Each fallback step is gated by budget and latency budgets and must report rollback delta.

5) Splice/patch mechanism: when rerouted output diverges from a previously soft-committed prefix, runtime computes a minimal edit patch and exposes an event: "soft-commit-corrected". SDKs will be extended to surface this event so callers can reconcile state incrementally.

Telemetry & acceptance metrics:
- acceptance_rate(route): fraction of requests that reach fast commit.
- soft_commit_rate: fraction that used soft-commit.
- early_commit_precision: fraction of fast-committed tokens that match gold tokens at next-k positions (k configurable).
- rollback_cost: mean additional latency and token delta when a rollback occurs.
- fallback_frequency: counts per fallback tier per 10k requests.
- kernel_match_miss: percent of times the cached fingerprint did not match and a full re-eval occurred.

Instrumentation plan:
- Add per-request traces capturing: kernel_fingerprint, p_accept, commit_decision, fallback_taken, rollback_delta, and splice_patch_size.
- Dashboard: Route-level acceptance_rate, rollback_cost P50/P95, fallback_frequency heatmap by model and region.
- Alerting: fallback_frequency > threshold or rollback_cost P95 exceeds configured SLOs.

Operational safety and user experience:
- Default thresholds are conservative for free-tier/unknown routes and aggressive for enterprise routes with dedicated capacity.
- Soft-commit tags allow client libraries to display intermediate text but the runtime will attempt transparent corrections; SDKs must surface correction events.
- Rollback transparency: when a rollback exceeds a safety delta (e.g., >8 tokens changed), we escalate to the operations channel and annotate logs for postmortem.

Compatibility and API changes:
- Minimal API surface change: responses gain an optional "commit_status" field and an events list with entries like "soft-commit" and "soft-commit-corrected". Both fields are optional strings.
- SDK patch to surface events and provide a granular subscription callback (onCorrection).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (lab): implement arbiter in runtime shim; run synthetic evals against existing acceptance datasets. Run microbenchmarks to ensure p_accept inference cost <200us.
- Phase 2 (canary): route 1% traffic for internal customers, monitor telemetry and user-visible regressions.
- Phase 3 (gradual): expand to 10% then 50% with automated rollback if early_commit_precision falls below guardrail.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Arbiter integrated in runtime and passing unit/integration tests.
- p_accept inference latency <200 microseconds on target infra and memory overhead <2% per worker.
- Dashboards publish acceptance_rate and rollback_cost per route.
- Canary run (1%) for 72 hours with rollback_cost P95 < 250ms and early_commit_precision > 95% on control prompts.

Design links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Matcher+and+Gated+Commit+Design
- Eval harness (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/main/arbiter
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

Dependencies:
- ENG-703210: kernel-benchmarking-framework (must land benchmark caching)
- ENG-724511: sdk-events-surface (SDK callbacks for corrections)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Acceptance model complexity: simple logistic model versus small decision tree. Start linear and iterate.
- Soft-commit UX: how will downstream streaming consumers react to corrected tokens? Need product/SDK guidance.
- Telemetry volume: per-request traces increase cardinality; consider sampling.

Notes and rationale for novelty:
- The kernel matcher caches a per-(model,seq_bucket,device) micro-profile to avoid expensive kernel probes on short-lived requests. This reduces noise when sequences are short (common in chat use).
- Soft-commit + splice reduces visible jank compared to full rollback by favoring small localized corrections.
